pr_title: filter unknowns from simple lists and maps in sdk
pr_body:
While there was already a check in the sdk to filter unknowns from
validation, it missed the case where those were in simple lists and maps.

Fixes #21419

issue_context.title: TF 0.12 - TypeMap validation function gets placeholder values from variables
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version
```
Terraform v0.12.0
+ provider.kubernetes v1.7.0
```

### Terraform Configuration Files
<!--
Paste the relevant parts of your Terraform configuration between the ``` marks below.

For large Terraform configs, please use a service like Dropbox and share a link to the ZIP file. For security, you can also encrypt the files using our GPG public key.
-->

```hcl
variable "quota_pods" {
  default = 5
}
variable "quota_memory_request" {
  default = "4Gi"
}

resource "kubernetes_resource_quota" "resource" {
  metadata {
    name = "quota"
  }

  spec {
    hard = {
      pods              = var.quota_pods
      "requests.memory" = var.quota_memory_request

      #   pods = 5
      #   "requests.memory" = "4Gi"
    }
  }
}
```

### Debug Output
<!--
Full debug output can be obtained by running Terraform with the environment variable `TF_LOG=trace`. Please create a GitHub Gist containing the debug output. Please do _not_ paste the debug output in the issue, since debug output is long.

Debug output may contain sensitive information. Please review it before posting publicly, and if you are concerned feel free to encrypt the files using the HashiCorp security public key.
-->
https://gist.github.com/alexsomesan/2fe40bfee0f0a07d2d036ba1a2ee6f52

### Crash Output
<!--
If the console output indicates that Terraform crashed, please share a link to a GitHub Gist containing the output of the `crash.log` file.
-->
N/A

### Expected Behavior
<!--
What should have happened?
-->
Planning should execute successfully and display the plan output.

### Actual Behavior
<!--
What actually happened?
-->
Validation errors are shown that indicate the contents of the values in the `hard` map are not the ones passed in through the corresponding variables.
Further digging reveals that all the map's values are in fact the same UUID string.

### Steps to Reproduce
<!--
Please list the full steps required to reproduce the issue, for example:
1. `terraform init`
2. `terraform plan`
-->
1. `terraform init`
2. `terraform plan`

### Additional Context
<!--
Are there anything atypical about your situation that we should know? For example: is Terraform running in a wrapper script or in a CI system? Are you passing any unusual command line options or environment variables to opt-in to non-default behavior?
-->
When the same values are passed in as literals directly in the map block, the plan executes as expected and the plan output displays the correct values.
To reproduce, uncomment the two commented lines containing literals and comment out the existing ones.

<!--
Are there any other GitHub issues (open or closed) or Pull Requests that should be linked here? For example:

- #6017

-->
https://github.com/terraform-providers/terraform-provider-kubernetes/issues/452

review_comments:
Would this also trip up on a list of lists where the second level contains unknowns? I don't know that any provider has ever actually done that, but I think the schema would allow it. :thinking: 

I kinda remember seeing a helper function somewhere to recursively visit all of a data structure looking for `config.UnknownVariableValue`, which in our new world in Terraform Core was of course replaced by `cty`'s `IsWhollyKnown`. I wonder if we still have that old-school helper around somewhere to use here. HIL is the most likely place I'd expect to find it, since it would've needed it for its special behavior of flattening a collection containing unknowns down into a single unknown.

Yeah, I forgot that helper/schema accepts nested types in places, so just made the filter recursive.

There is a similar check already (probably multiple, and `UnknownAsNull` in cty), but the schema needs to have a value for required fields in order to validate, so we have to filter them later.
